title: Joining in with repeated refrains
keyIdea: Some stories have a line that comes back again and again, like 'Run, run, as fast as you can!' This is called a refrain. It uses the same words every time. When the reader stops and waits, it is your turn: say the line. Listen for the pattern, like someone saying Stop!, so you know when it is coming.
familyTip: Read a story with a refrain, like The Gingerbread Man. The second time the line comes, slow down and pause before it, and look at your child. Wait. Smile when they join in, and say it together if they do not yet.

visual.caption: Which story does each line come from? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Run, run, as fast as you can!
Little pig, little pig, let me come in!
Not by the hair on my chinny chin chin!

lab.caption: Flagship lab: join in at the pause, put the pattern in order, match lines to stories, keep the words the same, make Teddy's own line.

kid: The Gingerbread Man runs away. He shouts: Run, run, as fast as you can! Then a cow says: Stop! And he shouts it again.
A line that comes back again and again is a refrain. It has the same words every time.
When the reader stops and waits, that is your turn. Say the line! Big and loud, or soft and slow.
Every story has its own line. The pigs say: I'll huff and I'll puff! The goats hear: Who's that trip-trapping over my bridge?
adult: Ages 2 to 3. Development Matters (2021) Communication and Language asks children from birth to 3 to sing songs and say rhymes, and children aged 3 to 4 to anticipate key events and phrases in rhymes and stories. Joining in with a refrain builds listening, memory for language and phonological awareness, and leads towards retelling stories in the Reception ELG Comprehension. Key words: refrain, repetition, predictable text, anticipate.

Pick books with a strong repeated line, such as traditional tales or rhyming picture books. Read the line with the same rhythm and voice every time. On the second or third time, slow down and stop just before it, with a look that says your turn. Wait a few seconds. Praise any try, even one word.

Common mistakes: the adult does not leave a long enough pause; the child says the line at every page, not at the right moment; the words change each time (so it is not a refrain); mixing up lines from different stories; and saying only part of the line. Be careful to keep your own words exactly the same each time.

In the lab your child reads along and taps Join in only when the reader waits, puts meet, Stop and the line in order, matches four lines to their stories, picks the same words from changed ones, and makes Teddy's own refrain to join in with.

practice.prompt: The Gingerbread Man has run away from {n} animals. A new animal says: Stop! What does he shout next?
choices: Run, run, as fast as you can!
Walk, walk, as slow as you can!
practice.hint: His line is the same every time. What did he shout before?
practice.explain: After all {n} animals he shouts the same line: Run, run, as fast as you can!

practice.prompt: A story has {n} pages. The line comes on every page. How many times do you join in?
practice.hint: The line comes once on each page. Count the pages.
practice.explain: The line comes once on each of the {n} pages, so you join in {n} times.

practice.prompt: The reader stops and looks at you. What do you do?
choices: Say the line that comes back
practice.hint: When the reader waits, whose turn is it?
practice.explain: The pause is your turn. Say the line that keeps coming back.

practice.prompt: Which story says: I'll huff and I'll puff?
practice.explain: The wolf in the Three Little Pigs says: I'll huff and I'll puff!

practice.prompt: Do the words of a refrain change each time?
practice.hint: Think of Run, run, as fast as you can. Is it the same each time?
practice.explain: A refrain uses the same words every time. That is why you can join in.

choices: A line that comes back again and again
pool.hint: Think of a line you hear many times in one story.
pool.explain: A refrain is a line that comes back again and again, with the same words.

pool.prompt: In the Three Billy Goats Gruff, what does the troll shout?
choices: Who's that trip-trapping over my bridge?
Run, run, as fast as you can!
pool.hint: The goats go trip-trap over a bridge.
pool.explain: The troll shouts: Who's that trip-trapping over my bridge?

pool.prompt: The reader is on page {n}. Nobody has said Stop yet. Should you shout the line now?
choices: Yes, shout it on every page
pool.hint: When does the reader stop and wait?
pool.explain: On page {n} nobody has said Stop, so wait. The line comes at the pause, not on every page.

pool.prompt: Sam says: Run, as fast as you can. What did he miss?
pool.hint: The whole line is: Run, run, as fast as you can!
pool.explain: The line has run twice: Run, run, as fast as you can! Say the whole line.

pool.prompt: In the Little Red Hen, the hen asks: Who will help me? What does the dog say?
pool.hint: Nobody wants to help the hen.
pool.explain: Each animal says: Not I! That is the Little Red Hen's refrain.

pool.prompt: A cow says: Stop! Then a horse says: Stop! What comes after a horse says Stop?
choices: Run, run, as fast as you can!
pool.hint: What came after the cow said Stop?
pool.explain: Each Stop! is followed by the line: Run, run, as fast as you can!

pool.prompt: The wolf goes to {n} houses. He says I'll huff and I'll puff at each one. How many times does he say it?
pool.hint: He says it once at each house. Count the houses.
pool.explain: Once at each of the {n} houses, so he says it {n} times.

pool.prompt: Teddy's line is: Splash, splash, in we go! What does Teddy say the next time?
pool.hint: A refrain keeps the same words.
pool.explain: The refrain is the same each time: Splash, splash, in we go!

pool.prompt: How do you know the Gingerbread Man's line is coming?
pool.hint: What happens just before he runs away?
pool.explain: Each time someone says Stop!, the line comes next. The pattern tells you.
